tools.description: CALL THIS FIRST when working with calculator pricing! Returns comprehensive schema documentation for the 8-table Calculator Pricing Database on Supabase PostgreSQL. This is your MASTER REFERENCE for understanding the entire system. Returns: (1) Database overview with TWO SYSTEMS architecture explained, (2) All 8 table schemas with columns/types/constraints/indexes, (3) JSONB field structures and access patterns, (4) Foreign key relationships and data flow, (5) Query construction best practices, (6) 20+ copy-paste ready example queries, (7) Available pre-built queries DYNAMICALLY INJECTED from QueryLibrary, (8) Decision tree for when to use direct SQL vs pre-built queries vs API endpoints. Also includes data quality notes, migration history, and optimization strategies. Use this to learn the complete system before writing any queries.

workflow: Step 1: Call calculator_database_get_schema_guide() to get complete reference
Step 2: Review overview section to understand TWO SYSTEMS architecture
Step 3: Check available_queries list to see if pre-built query exists for your task
Step 4: If match found use execute_query_library() with that query name
Step 5: If no match review example_queries section for similar patterns
Step 6: Use query_patterns section to learn JSONB access syntax
Step 7: Write custom query using calculator_database_query()
Step 8: For updates use calculator_database_modify() with reason
best_practices: ALWAYS call this tool FIRST when working with calculator pricing
Check available_queries list BEFORE writing custom SQL
Use example queries as templates for your custom queries
Follow JSONB access patterns exactly (use ->> for text, ::numeric for numbers, @> for contains)
Always cast JSONB fields to appropriate types for sorting and filtering
Check is_active=TRUE when querying overrides for current values
Use array_agg() and json_build_object() to avoid N+1 queries
Include reason parameter when modifying data for audit trail
error_handling: Tool always succeeds and returns guide object
If QueryLibrary unavailable: available_queries will be empty list
If database connection fails: Guide still returns with schema documentation
